 Jaylen Waddle (concussion) was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice.
 Waddle exited the Broncos’ Week 9 game against the Panthers with a concussion. He had time to work through the protocol with a Week 10 bye and is now back to practicing at the start of Week 11. Given his full participant listing, Waddle is trending to play this week against the Raiders. He has had a disappointing fantasy season and should be in the WR3 ranks for Week 11.
 -  Aditya Fuldeore

 Jaylen Waddle suffered a concussion in the Broncos’ Week 9 game against the Panthers and will not return. 
 Waddle was listed as questionable in the first half but then ruled out to begin the third. It’s another nightmare development for Waddle in his first Broncos season, as he has struggled for both 100 percent health and productive box scores. Today’s injury came as Waddle skied for a target over the middle of the field and got high/lowed. He had just one grab for 22 yards before departing. The only good news is the Broncos are on bye for Week 10, meaning Waddle might not miss any game time beyond this afternoon. 
 Jaylen Waddle 
 DEN 
 Wide Receiver 
 #17 
 Jaylen Waddle (chest) is practicing in full for Week 9 against the Panthers. 
 Waddle played through a questionable tag with this injury last week, catching 3-of-6 targets for 39 yards and one touchdown against the Chiefs. He apparently made it through the contest without re-injuring himself and can be started as a WR3 this week against the Panthers. 
 Jaylen Waddle 
 DEN 
 Wide Receiver 
 #17 
 Jaylen Waddle caught 3-of-6 targets for 39 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 8 win over the Chiefs. 
 Starting with the positive, Waddle found the end zone for the second time this year and got going over the middle of the field with a 35-yard missile from Nix early in the second quarter. It’s his longest catch since Week 2, when he erupted for 138 yards on eight receptions, including a 49-yarder. On the downside, Waddle managed a pedestrian 19 percent target share and finished third on the team in receiving. He found the end zone and still scored a grand total of 12.9 PPR points. The Broncos’ offense is still a work in progress, even if today was a step in the right direction. Waddle will get another week in the WR3 mix when the Broncos take on the Panthers. 
 Jaylen Waddle 
 DEN 
 Wide Receiver 
 #17 
 Jaylen Waddle (shoulder) is active for Week 8 against the Chiefs. 
 Left tackle Garrett Boles and EDGE Zach Allen are also active. All Broncos players who were questionable for Week 8 are active. After a disappointing two months to start the year, Waddle is at the back of the WR3 ranks for Week 8. Inactive for the Broncos are S Talana Hufanga, QB Sam Ehlinger, OL Gavin Ortega, DL Jordan Jackson, DL Tyler Oneydim, OL Kage Casey, and TE Dallen Bentley. 
 Jaylen Waddle 
 DEN 
 Wide Receiver 
 #17 
 ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Jaylen Waddle (chest) is “trending toward playing” in Week 8 against the Chiefs. 
 Waddle suffered the chest injury late in the Broncos’ Week 7 win over the Cardinals and a doomed trick play. He was leveled by Josh Sweat several yards behind the line of scrimmage. The Broncos held him out of Wednesday’s practice before giving him two limited sessions and a questionable tag. Though we suspect he is on some form of a snap count, it looks like Waddle is giving it a go. Already struggling to put up WR3 fantasy numbers, we’re regarding him as a high-risk FLEX play versus Kansas City.

 #17 
 Jaylen Waddle (chest) is questionable for Denver’s Week 8 game against the Chiefs. 
 Waddle got in two limited sessions after missing practice on Wednesday. It feels like he’s on the optimistic side of questionable given the trend line, though of course you would have preferred to see a full session somewhere in here. It’s also possible he winds up on a snap count, so we’ll see if any insiders dig up anything on that this weekend.

 Jaylen Waddle (chest) was limited in Thursday’s practice. 
 Waddle aggravated an existing chest injury on a trick play late in the fourth quarter of Week 7. A return to the practice field, in any capacity, Thursday keeps the door open for him to be available to play the Chiefs in Week 8, although fantasy managers are likely looking for an excuse to bench the over-hyped receiver. It would be prudent to look at other viable options in a difficult matchup.

 Jaylen Waddle (chest) did not practice on Wednesday. 
 Earlier today, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported that Waddle’s status for Week 8 against the Chiefs has not been determined. The Broncos’ No. 1 wide receiver aggravated his preexisting chest injury in Week 7 against the Cardinals. Backup plans should be made at this time. 
 Jaylen Waddle 
 DEN 
 Wide Receiver 
 #17 
 NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said Jaylen Waddle suffered a chest injury and his Week 8 status has not been determined. 
 Waddle left Sunday’s game against the Cardinals with the chest injury. It was, according to Rapoport, an “aggravation of his previous chest injury.” Waddle could try to practice later this week, but would appear to be iffy unless he can log a practice session by Friday. If Waddle is sidelined this week against the Chiefs, Courtland Sutton would likely see more targets and become an interesting flex option against a tough KC secondary. Sutton over the past four weeks leads Denver in air yards and has the second most targets behind Waddle. 
 Jaylen Waddle 
 DEN 
 Wide Receiver 
 #17 
 Jaylen Waddle left Week 7’s game against the Cardinals with an apparent chest injury. 
 Up by 14, Sean Payton dialed up a trick play for Waddle, giving him a pitch as Waddle came across the formation. Waddle bobbled the ball and was clobbered by Josh Sweat. He writhed in pain while holding his left shoulder. Trainers came onto the field and eventually walked him into the locker room. With less than four minutes on the clock at the time of his departure, we don’t expect to see him again today. Waddle’s day ends with four catches for 48 yards on seven targets.

 Baker Mayfield (foot) returned to practice on Thursday.
 Mayfield did not practice Wednesday after injuring his foot ahead of the Bucs’ Week 10 bye. It initially looked like he would miss his Week 11 game against the Lions. Now he might be on the right side of questionable. Mayfield was spotted going through ball security drills and hopping over pads early in the practice. He certainly looked like a quarterback who was preparing to play in a few days. Mayfield hasn’t been all that productive this year, but he would still be an upgrade over Jalon Daniels. This is a situation to monitor heading into the weekend. 
 -  Kyle Dvorchak 
 Source:  Greg Auman

 The Baltimore Ravens sent Marlon Humphrey home and he will be inactive for Week 11.
 Humphrey was asked what the city of Baltimore was good at making on his personal podcast, The Marlon Humphrey Show. He jokingly responded, “They’re the best at making criminals.” Humphrey has since apologized for the disparaging remark, but the team is dismissing him for the week after a wave of backlash. He could potentially return in Week 12 against Houston.

 49ers GM John Lynch said “there’s a chance” Mike Evans (Achilles) practices on Thursday.
 We’ll know more in a few hours, but even a chance at practicing is a small step in the right direction for Evans. The veteran wideout hasn’t played since Week 6 because of his Achilles tendinitis. We still expect this to be a ramp-up week of practice for him before returning in Week 12, but there’s at least an outside shot of him suiting up on Sunday.

 NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Christian Kirk underwent a successful meniscus surgery. 
 Rapoport didn’t give any details on Kirk’s timeline to return. We suspect he is done for the season. Kirk missed most of the season with a hamstring injury. He returned for one game, didn’t record any stats, and then injured his knee. Kirk signed a one-year deal with the 49ers in the offseason. He will be stuck taking another prove-it deal if he’s healthy when free agency starts in the offseason. 
 -  Kyle Dvorchak

 Commanders signed WR Malik Heath to the practice squad.
 Heath worked out for the Commanders Wednesday and signed to the practice squad. He caught 31 passes for 308 yards and three touchdowns over the past three seasons with the Packers and spent some time with the Falcons as well last season. The Commanders add Heath as receiving depth for the practice squad.

 Daiyan Henley (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
 Henley infamously was sent back to the Chargers after a reported trade with Denver fell through due to a failed physical. He returned to play in the Chargers’ Week 10 win over the Ravens, but now misses the first practice of the week with a knee issue. Given he has been playing through soreness, Henley’s absence may just be load management after a Monday game. Henley still has a chance to play in Week 11 with practices later in the week.

 Ladd McConkey (back) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
 McConkey has been dealing with the back injury for two weeks now, sitting out the Chargers’ last two games. He continues to deal with a various set of injuries and is a wild card when it comes to playing on game days. A limited designation at least gives fantasy managers hope that he will play in Week 11 against the Jets, though McConkey has fallen to unreliable WR3 status at this point of the season.

 Charlie Kolar (concussion) did not practice Wednesday.
 Kolar seemingly came out of the Chargers’ first win of the season with a concussion, though he was on the field up until making the game-sealing catch on the last drive. He will need to clear concussion protocol in order to be eligible for Week 11 against the Jets. Also not practicing was WR Brenen Thompson (hamstring). Neither player has fantasy impact, though Kolar’s blocking is important for a Chargers team with a banged-up offensive line.
